> **What this case shows** — the [Welch case](../eeg-bandpower-welch-eegmmidb/index.qmd) gave the
> alpha *power* and the [spectrogram case](../eeg-spectrogram-scipy-eegmmidb/index.qmd) its *time
> course*. **Coherence** gives its *spatial structure*: how consistently two channels share a
> phase-and-amplitude relationship at each frequency. On the eight parieto-occipital channels of
> real eyes-closed EEG, `eegCoherence` reproduces `scipy.signal.coherence` **bit-for-bit**
> (max |diff| ~**2e-16** across all 28 pairs) once the conventions match. And the finding: posterior
> alpha coherence is **high** (mean **0.63**, peaking **0.90** between adjacent occipital channels
> PO3–O1) — the eyes-closed alpha rhythm is spatially synchronized across the posterior scalp.

::: {.callout-tip title="The recipe you'll learn"}
**Workflow** — for spectral connectivity: `eegCoherence(pe, band = c(8, 13))` → a channel × channel
coherence matrix, band-averaged.
**Way of thinking** — coherence is a *ratio* of the cross-spectrum to the auto-spectra, so it lives
in [0, 1] and (crucially) the window normalization cancels — two implementations that share the
window and detrend agree to machine epsilon. But high coherence between nearby electrodes is
partly **volume conduction**, not proof of coupling — reach for imaginary coherence when that
matters.
**Ecosystem usage** — `PhysioEEG::eegCoherence()`; `method = "imaginary"` to suppress the zero-lag
(volume-conduction) component.
:::

## Proposition

On real eyes-closed posterior EEG, `eegCoherence` reproduces `scipy.signal.coherence` bit-for-bit
(max |diff| ~2e-16 over all 28 pairs); and posterior alpha coherence is high (mean 0.63, peak 0.90).

## Question & goal

**The question is fidelity and structure: does the ecosystem's coherence equal
`scipy.signal.coherence` — and how spatially synchronized is the eyes-closed alpha rhythm?** The
goal is a machine-precision certification over every channel pair and a read of the posterior alpha
network.

## Challenge & approach

Magnitude-squared coherence is Cxy = |Sxy|²/(Sxx·Syy) from the Welch-averaged cross/auto spectra.
Because it is a *ratio*, the window normalization cancels — so the only conventions that matter are
the window shape, the segmenting, and the detrend. The op uses a symmetric Hann window, matched
window length + hop, and no detrend; we point scipy at exactly those and compare the full matrix.

```
EEG 8 posterior ch (eegmmidb, 160 Hz) → eegCoherence(band = 8-13 Hz) → 8 × 8 coherence matrix
                    vs scipy.signal.coherence (symmetric Hann, matched window/overlap, detrend=False) → bit-exact (~2e-16)
                                    mean 0.63, peak 0.90 (PO3-O1) → the alpha rhythm is spatially synchronized
```

## Data

**EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database (eegmmidb, PhysioNet)**: subject **S002**, run **R02
(eyes-closed)**, the eight **parieto-occipital** channels (PO7, PO3, POz, PO4, PO8, O1, Oz, O2), 10 s
at 160 Hz — subset from the same git-tracked root the
[Welch](../eeg-bandpower-welch-eegmmidb/index.qmd),
[spectrogram](../eeg-spectrogram-scipy-eegmmidb/index.qmd), and
[Hjorth](../eeg-hjorth-eegmmidb/index.qmd) cases use. Details in
[`artifacts/data_sources.json`](artifacts/data_sources.json).

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| posterior channels × pairs | **8 × 28** |
| op vs `scipy.signal.coherence` (max \|diff\|) | **2e-16** (bit-exact) |

The op equals scipy to machine epsilon over every pair, and the posterior alpha rhythm is highly
synchronized. Values trace to [`artifacts/coherence_summary.csv`](artifacts/coherence_summary.csv).

## Conclusion

The ecosystem's coherence *is* `scipy.signal.coherence` — bit-for-bit over every pair, because the
coherence ratio cancels the window normalization and the window + detrend conventions match — so the
connectivity op is certified against the reference; and on real eyes-closed EEG it shows the
posterior alpha rhythm as spatially synchronized, cross-consistent with the Welch (high posterior
alpha power), spectrogram (sustained alpha), and Hjorth (low posterior mobility) cases on the same
data. The transferable takeaway: **coherence is a normalized ratio — pin the window and detrend and
it matches to machine epsilon; but magnitude-squared coherence is inflated by volume conduction, so
read it as an upper bound on coupling and switch to imaginary coherence when you need the true
network.**

## Open questions

- Magnitude-squared coherence cannot separate genuine coupling from **volume conduction** (one
  source seen by two electrodes at zero lag). The op's **imaginary coherence** (`method =
  "imaginary"`) keeps only the lagged component, which volume conduction cannot produce; computing
  it across the montage — and contrasting eyes-closed with eyes-open — would isolate the true
  posterior alpha network from the shared-source inflation. *Documented, not escalated.*

## Using this in your own analysis

| Step | Function | Package |
|---|---|---|
| magnitude-squared coherence matrix | `eegCoherence(method = "coherence")` | PhysioEEG |
| imaginary coherence (volume-conduction-robust) | `eegCoherence(method = "imaginary")` | PhysioEEG |
| band power (the sibling view) | `bandPower(method = "welch")` | PhysioAnalysis |

**Choosing the parameters.**

- **band** — the frequency band to average coherence over (here 8–13 Hz alpha); coherence is
  frequency-resolved, so pick the band your hypothesis names.
- **window_sec** — the Welch segment length in seconds (here 2 s → more segments = more stable
  coherence, but coarser frequency resolution).
- **method** — `"coherence"` (magnitude-squared, this case) vs `"imaginary"` (keeps only the lagged
  component, robust to volume conduction).
- **the conventions** — coherence is a ratio, so the window normalization cancels; only the window
  shape, segmenting, and detrend must match across tools.

**The recipe, copy-runnable:**

```r
library(PhysioEEG)

res <- eegCoherence(pe, method = "coherence", window_sec = 2, band = c(8, 13))
cm  <- S4Vectors::metadata(res)$connectivity$matrix   # channel x channel coherence

# equals scipy.signal.coherence bit-for-bit (max |diff| ~2e-16) with matched conventions:
# get_window("hann", nperseg, fftbins = FALSE), matched noverlap, detrend = FALSE.
```

[`artifacts/coherence_summary.csv`](artifacts/coherence_summary.csv), and [`audit.py`](audit.py)
